stream_request (llm.py:105-110) uses `with self._client.messages.stream(**payload) as stream`, iterates `stream.text_stream`, and calls `stream.get_final_message()`. The fake (tests/unit/test_llm_sampling_options.py:47-63) returns an object with __enter__ (returns self), __exit__, a text_stream iterable (empty tuple), and get_final_message() returning a namespace with content/stop_reason/usage, which is all stream_request and _parse_message_content touch. This matches the Anthropic SDK shape: messages.stream() returns a MessageStreamManager whose sync __enter__ yields a MessageStream exposing text_stream and get_final_message(). I did not read the SDK source in the view; this rests on my knowledge of the SDK. The sync context manager matches the sync client used.

tests/unit/test_llm_sampling_options.py:69 sets svc._client = SimpleNamespace(messages=messages), where messages is a recording fake whose create(**kwargs) just stores the kwargs (lines 43-45). This bypasses the anthropic SDK entirely, so request building never runs. The assertion at line 110 (kwargs['extra_body'] == {'output_config': {'effort': 'high'}}) only proves the kwarg is passed to the SDK call. The SDK's own merge of extra_body into the JSON body happens elsewhere: anthropic/_base_client.py:2386-2387 puts it in options['extra_json'], and line 536 merges it. The test does not exercise that code. So the fake does not exercise the same payload path as the real client, and the claim's first half is false. The test gap is real but low-impact. The SDK's extra_body handling is standard, so the weakness is a limited-coverage issue.
